2025-10-16 | Lab 8" author: "Jess Helmer" footer: "[jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026](https://jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026/)" format: revealjs: code-link: true slide-number: true code-line-numbers: false theme: ../../gt-theme.scss width: 1200 execute: echo: true dpi: 600 freeze: auto knitr: opts_chunk: dev: svg --- ## Outline - ANOVA review - Frequentist ANOVA - Bayesian ANOVA ::: {.cell} ::: # ANOVA ## [**An**]{style="color:#b04c19"}alysis [**o**]{style="color:#5a55fa"}f [**Va**]{style="color:#dfc127"}riance (**[AN]{style="color:#b04c19"}[O]{style="color:#5a55fa"}[VA]{style="color:#dfc127"}**) [**An**]{style="color:#b04c19"}alysis [**o**]{style="color:#5a55fa"}f [**Va**]{style="color:#dfc127"}riance (**[AN]{style="color:#b04c19"}[O]{style="color:#5a55fa"}[VA]{style="color:#dfc127"}**) Method of understanding how categorical variables are related to a continuous outcome of interest Compares *between groups* to *within groups* variance to jointly compare multiple means ## ANOVA: Partitioning Variance **Total Sum of Squared Errors:** error term around the grand mean $$ SS_{total} = \sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2 $$ If we have outcomes separated into different groups (e.g., control, treatment A, treatment B), can partition $SS_{total}$ into *between groups sums of squares* $SS_B$ and *within groups sums of squares* $SS_W$ $$ SS_{total} = SS_B + SS_W $$ [So, with $j$ indexing $J$ total groups and $i$ indexing $I$ people within a group, we can write $SS_{total}$ as...]{.fragment} ## ANOVA: Partitioning Variance **Total Sum of Squared Errors:** error term around the grand mean $$ SS_{total} = \sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{i=1}^I (x_{ij} - \bar{x})^2 $$ :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Between-Group Sum of Squares:** error between the group mean and the grand mean $$ SS_{B} = \sum_{j=1}^J n_j (\bar{x_{j}} - \bar{x})^2 $$ ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Within-Group Sum of Squares:** error between observations and their group mean $$ SS_{W} = \sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{i=1}^I (x_{ij} - \bar{x_{j}})^2 $$ ::: :::: ## Partitioning Variance ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-12-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=864} ::: ::: ## Partitioning Variance: $SS_B$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-13-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=864} ::: ::: ## Partitioning Variance: $SS_W$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-14-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=864} ::: ::: ## Partitioning Variance Ratio of $SS_B$ to $SS_W$ If $SS_B >> SS_W$, good model. Easy to predict differences based on groups. If $SS_B \approx SS_W$, less good model. Not easy to predict differences based on groups. $$ F \propto \frac{\text{between-group variance}}{\text{within-group variance}} $$ ## ANOVA: $F$ :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Mean Square Between** $MS_B = \frac{SS_B}{J - 1} = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^J n_j (\bar{x_{j}} - \bar{x})^2}{J - 1}$ ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Mean Square Within** $MS_W = \frac{SS_W}{N - J} = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{i=1}^I (x_{ij} - \bar{x})^2}{N - J}$ ::: ::::
$$ F = \frac{MS_B}{MS_W} $$ ## ANOVA: Hypotheses $H_0$: $\sigma^2_B = 0$ $H_1$: $\sigma^2_B \neq 0$ ::: fragment Equivalent to: $H_0$: $\mu_1 = \mu_2 = ... = \mu_J$ $H_1$: not $H_0$ ::: ## Penguins ANOVA Example :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} **Chinstrap** ![](https://www.secretatlas.com/assets/handbook/antarctica-destination-micro-guide/half-moon-island/full-length-photograph-of-a-chinstrap-penguin-half-moon-island-south-shetland-islands-antarctica-shutterstock-secret-atlas.jpg) ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} **Adelie** ![](https://res.cloudinary.com/enchanting/q_70,f_auto,w_1024,h_683,c_fit/quark-web/2024/09/SamEdmonds20-20Adelie20closeup202.jpg) ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} **Gentoo** ![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c5/2020-11_Kerguelen_Islands_-_Gentoo_penguin_06_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original) ::: :::: ## Penguins ANOVA Examples ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palmerpenguins) ``` ::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} glimpse(penguins) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 344 Columns: 8 $ species Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adelie, Adel… $ island Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgersen, Torgerse… $ bill_length_mm 39.1, 39.5, 40.3, NA, 36.7, 39.3, 38.9, 39.2, 34.1, … $ bill_depth_mm 18.7, 17.4, 18.0, NA, 19.3, 20.6, 17.8, 19.6, 18.1, … $ flipper_length_mm 181, 186, 195, NA, 193, 190, 181, 195, 193, 190, 186… $ body_mass_g 3750, 3800, 3250, NA, 3450, 3650, 3625, 4675, 3475, … $ sex male, female, female, NA, female, male, female, male… $ year 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007… ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 344 × 8 species island bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm body_mass_g 1 Adelie Torgersen 39.1 18.7 181 3750 2 Adelie Torgersen 39.5 17.4 186 3800 3 Adelie Torgersen 40.3 18 195 3250 4 Adelie Torgersen NA NA NA NA 5 Adelie Torgersen 36.7 19.3 193 3450 6 Adelie Torgersen 39.3 20.6 190 3650 7 Adelie Torgersen 38.9 17.8 181 3625 8 Adelie Torgersen 39.2 19.6 195 4675 9 Adelie Torgersen 34.1 18.1 193 3475 10 Adelie Torgersen 42 20.2 190 4250 # ℹ 334 more rows # ℹ 2 more variables: sex , year ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: # Frequentist ANOVA ## ANOVA: R function `aov(y ~ grouping_var, data = data)` ::: subpoint-narrow ○ `y` = outcome ::: ::: subpoint-narrow ○ `grouping_var` = name of grouping variable ::: ::: subpoint-narrow ○ `data` = dataframe that includes `grouping_var` and `y` ::: Very similar syntax to `lm(y ~ predictor)` (and you can think of it similarly) Uses dummy coding by default `summary(model)` ## ANOVA: Example ::: fragment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_cleaned <- penguins |> filter_out(when_any(is.na(flipper_length_mm), is.na(species))) flipper_model <- aov(flipper_length_mm ~ species, data = penguins_cleaned) summary(flipper_model) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F) species 2 52473 26237 594.8 <2e-16 *** Residuals 339 14953 44 --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: [Huge $F$-statistic!]{.fragment} [We reject the null in favor of the alternative that there is significant variation between penguin species in flipper length]{.fragment} ## Effect Sizes: Example :::: {.columns} ::: {.column .fragment width="50%"} $\eta^2$ ::: fragment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} effectsize::eta_squared(flipper_model) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # Effect Size for ANOVA Parameter | Eta2 | 95% CI ------------------------------- species | 0.78 | [0.75, 1.00] - One-sided CIs: upper bound fixed at [1.00]. ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} $\omega^2$ ::: fragment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} effectsize::omega_squared(flipper_model) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # Effect Size for ANOVA Parameter | Omega2 | 95% CI --------------------------------- species | 0.78 | [0.75, 1.00] - One-sided CIs: upper bound fixed at [1.00]. ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Assumptions: Normality and Outliers ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-21-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_cleaned |> ggplot(aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = species, color = species)) + geom_violin(alpha = 0.5, color = NA) + geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, outliers = F) + geom_jitter(alpha = 0.4, shape = 16, size = 3) + stat_summary(geom = "point", fun = mean, size = 2.5) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("#b04c19", "#5a55fa", "#dfc127")) + scale_color_manual(values = scales::col_darker(c("#b04c19", "#5a55fa", "#dfc127"), 15)) + labs(x = "Species", y = "Flipper Length (mm)") + guides(y = guide_axis(cap = "both"), x = guide_axis(cap = "both")) + coord_flip() + theme_classic(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: ::: # Bayesian ANOVA ## Bayesian ANOVA: Example Can use `stan_glm()` within `{rstanarm}` again. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(rstanarm) flipper_model_bayes <- stan_glm( flipper_length_mm ~ species, data = penguins_cleaned, family = "gaussian" ) summary(flipper_model_bayes) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Model Info: function: stan_glm family: gaussian [identity] formula: flipper_length_mm ~ species algorithm: sampling sample: 4000 (posterior sample size) priors: see help('prior_summary') observations: 342 predictors: 3 Estimates: mean sd 10% 50% 90% (Intercept) 190.0 0.6 189.3 190.0 190.7 speciesChinstrap 5.8 1.0 4.6 5.8 7.1 speciesGentoo 27.2 0.8 26.2 27.2 28.3 sigma 6.7 0.3 6.3 6.7 7.0 Fit Diagnostics: mean sd 10% 50% 90% mean_PPD 200.9 0.5 200.3 200.9 201.6 The mean_ppd is the sample average posterior predictive distribution of the outcome variable (for details see help('summary.stanreg')). MCMC diagnostics mcse Rhat n_eff (Intercept) 0.0 1.0 4249 speciesChinstrap 0.0 1.0 4475 speciesGentoo 0.0 1.0 4601 sigma 0.0 1.0 4672 mean_PPD 0.0 1.0 4031 log-posterior 0.0 1.0 1809 For each parameter, mcse is Monte Carlo standard error, n_eff is a crude measure of effective sample size, and Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence Rhat=1). ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} With dummy coding, ::: subpoint-narrow ○ $\beta_0 = $ mean of reference group (here, $\mu_\text{Adelie}$) ::: ::: subpoint-narrow ○ $\beta_1 = $ difference between target group and reference group (here, $\mu_\text{Chinstrap} - \mu_\text{Adelie}$) ::: ::: subpoint-narrow ○ $\beta_2 = $ difference between target group and reference group (here, $\mu_\text{Gentoo} - \mu_\text{Adelie}$) ::: ::: :::: ## Check Diagnostics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} posterior::summarise_draws(flipper_model_bayes, "mean", "sd", "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 4 × 6 variable mean sd rhat ess_bulk ess_tail 1 (Intercept) 190. 0.553 1.00 4265. 2765. 2 speciesChinstrap 5.84 0.976 1.000 4472. 3011. 3 speciesGentoo 27.2 0.815 1.00 4603. 2841. 4 sigma 6.66 0.260 1.00 4694. 2813. ``` ::: ::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bayesplot::mcmc_trace(flipper_model_bayes) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-26-1.svg){width=576} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bayesplot::mcmc_rank_overlay(flipper_model_bayes) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-27-1.svg){width=576} ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Look at Posterior Predictive :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-28-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=768} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bayesplot::ppc_dens_overlay_grouped( y = penguins_cleaned$flipper_length_mm, yrep = posterior_predict(flipper_model_bayes, draws = 50), group = penguins_cleaned$species ) ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-30-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} posterior_predictive_data <- bayesplot::ppc_data( y = penguins_cleaned$flipper_length_mm, yrep = posterior_predict(flipper_model_bayes, draws = 50), group = penguins_cleaned$species ) original_data <- posterior_predictive_data |> filter(is_y) model_draws <- posterior_predictive_data |> filter_out(is_y) model_draws |> ggplot() + ggridges::geom_density_ridges( aes(x = value, y = group, group = interaction(group, rep_id)), fill = NA, color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.25, scale = 1, rel_min_height = 0 ) + ggridges::geom_density_ridges( data = original_data, aes(x = value, y = group), fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8, scale = 1, rel_min_height = 0 ) + labs(x = "Flipper length (mm)", y = NULL) + ggridges::theme_ridges() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## <script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
